newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s end lower after sharp selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s end lower after sharp selloff.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mostly lower, with a computer-driven selloff pushing June Standard & Poor's 500s sharply lower in the afternoon, traders and floor analysts said.

"The market could have done this on Friday," said Daniel Riley, director of institutional trading at Chicago Execution Corp, adding that expirations-related buying kept prices afloat on Friday and inside Thursday's ranges.
However, Monday's late sell-off drove June S&Ps out of Friday's ranges. Sell-stop orders were heavy at Friday's pit low of 766.70, they said.
"We are gradually slipping here," one floor trader said when June cracked through the 768.50 level. "We are progressively hitting sell-stops."

June S&Ps knocked through last Thursday's low of 764.30 amid continued arbitrage buy and sell programs. Program trading was light and spotty throughout the day, and traders estimated lower-than-average volume.
They said the Passover holidays may have contributed to the thin trade.
Arbitrage sell programs were seen at a premium of 4.00 points, and arbitrage buy programs were 5.80 over.
Several traders said the market was still smarting from Sir John Templeton's comments on Friday.
Templeton told a group of investors to be prepared for the biggest bear market in U.S. stocks since the Great Depression. He estimated the market was likely to drop as much as 40 percent or more.

One analyst said on Reuters Financial Television that the tone in cash S&Ps remains constructive as long as prices remain above the January 2 low of 729.55. Cash S&Ps have held above that level, having retreated to 733.54 on Monday, April 14.
"From a technical perspective that low has not been taken out, which is constructive," Hans Kashyap, an analyst with Analytic Research Corp, said on RFTV on Monday afternoon.

June S&Ps, however, have fallen through the January 2 low of 740.00. The contract hit 736.70 on April 14, and its decline towards support at 758.00 on Monday led some floor traders to look for a retest of the 740.00 level.
The 740.00 level coincides with the contract's 200-day moving average at 740.70.

At the end of pit trade, June S&P 500s were down 6.10 points at 764.15, KCBT Value Lines fell 7.60 to 682.90, Nikkeis rose 135.0 to 18,565.0, Midcap 400s were off 3.20 to 250.05, NYSE Composites lost 4.00 to 400.70, Russell 2000s were down 4.90 at 338.70, and Nasdaq 100s were down 13.00 to 809.25.
